candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite unlike fractional parts as equivalent fractions before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S02, and C.S01 all describe creating a common denominator/LCD and converting fractions to equivalent forms prior to subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a mixed number with an improper fractional part into an equivalent standard mixed number before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S01 and C.S02 are direct matches; A.S02 is broader but includes this same normalization of mixed numbers with improper fractional parts, so it aligns here for that concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Express a whole number as a whole part plus a zero fractional part with an appropriate denominator so it can be subtracted alongside fractions or mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S04 and C.S03 match exactly. A does not separate this from broader operand normalization, so no distinct A-only skill maps here.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers once the forms are aligned.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include the same core subtraction operation after normalization and denominator alignment are complete.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as denominator-over-denominator fractional units and adjust the whole part when the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative or insufficient.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04, B.S05, and C.S05 all describe borrowing/regrouping across a mixed number by converting one whole into fractional units.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the result to lowest terms and remove any zero fractional part so the answer is expressed in simplest form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe post-subtraction simplification, including fraction reduction and converting zero-fraction results to whole numbers.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Assemble the computed whole-number and fractional parts into the final mixed number, fraction, or integer answer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S06 and B.S07 both isolate recombining parts into a final answer. C does not separate this as its own skill and appears to absorb it into subtraction or simplification.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks show strong agreement on the main subtraction workflow: denominator matching, mixed-number normalization, subtraction, borrowing/regrouping, and simplification. The main structural differences are that Expert A combines two preprocessing ideas under a broader normalization skill, while Experts B and C split them into separate skills: normalizing improper mixed numbers versus rewriting a whole number as a mixed form with 0 fractional part. Expert C also does not isolate a separate final recombination skill, whereas Experts A and B do.
